content.comment_body: Hello, Where can I locate the hardware configuration for [product_name] in the software? In the [product_name] [version_no] software, I can see hardware configuration. If a module is damaged, should I replace it with another of the same type?

Hello, From my experience, there isn’t a hardware configuration for DI/DO modules as there is in [product_name] [version_no], apart from HMI or similar devices. You can replace modules without issues.

In [product_name], hardware configuration is not present as in [product_name] [version_no]. For instance, in [product_name] [article_no], the first digital inputs (I1-I8) are on the basic module. On the first digital expansion module, you get I9-I12 (DM8) or I9-I16 (DM16). Similarly, digital outputs Q1-Q4 are on the basic module, and Q5-Q8 (DM8) or Q5-Q12 (DM16) on the first expansion module.
To understand how expansion modules are arranged and addressed, refer to the attached documentation.
Hello, Yes, swap modules with the same number and type of inputs/outputs to maintain functionality.
Hello, If you want identical behavior, use modules with corresponding specifications.
If you have two DM8 modules consecutively, you can replace both with one DM16.
Hello, What happens if you change a digital 8-input module for a digital 16-input module?
Hello, You gain 8 more digital inputs in this case.
You can substitute two DM8 modules with a single DM16, and this requires no changes in the program.
DM8 provides 4 inputs and 4 outputs. DM16 offers 8 inputs and 8 outputs. Note, there is no expansion module with 16 inputs; the maximum is 8.
Please remember: For [product_name] [article_no], the maximum digital inputs are 24, digital outputs 20, analog inputs 8, and analog outputs 8.
Hi, For analog input usage from the base module, if I use 2 analog inputs (I7 & I8), on the next expansion module, will the first input be I9 or I7? Thank you.

Initially: Digital expansion modules only offer digital inputs, not analog. The number of analog inputs depends on settings. In the file properties (File > Properties > Offline settings > I/O settings), you can select how many analog inputs are activated on the basic module. If all analog inputs on the base are off, the first expansion module starts at AI1; if two are activated on the base, the expansion starts at AI3; if four, at AI5.
Thank you for your quick reply. My question relates to DI numbering: If I define two analog inputs for the base module (displacing I7 and I8), will the next DI on the expansion module be I7 or I9?
On the next digital expansion module, the first digital input will be I9, regardless of the analog inputs activated on the base module.

analysis.insight_summary: Participants highlight that, unlike more complex PLCs such as [product_name] [version_no], there's no dedicated hardware configuration area for [product_name] modules in the programming software. Module changes are simple—just replace with the same type, and the addressing for expansion modules happens automatically. Questions focused on hardware flexibility (like increasing input capacity), and users appreciate the simple swap process, noting the difference from other PLCs.
analysis.user_expectations: Users are looking for a hardware configuration tool or interface for [product_name] modules comparable to what exists in [product_name] [version_no], as well as straightforward replacement procedures for damaged modules.
